limitations: Finite synchronized bursts, three fresh-server repeats; no sustained arrivals or maximum-capacity claim.
Prepared peers and server compete for the same two-vCPU Linux VM; private IPv4 loopback, not a two-host network benchmark.
Only fake-TLS TCP/UDP and QUIC-shaped UDP; other carriers, IPv6 AUTH and rejected-login throughput remain OPEN.
Handshake timer starts before ClientHello send, after socket connect and key/ClientHello generation; excludes process startup and server TUN setup.
AUTH timer includes encryption/send, network, server proof/credential checks, Argon2 permit queue, session admission and verified reply; not pure Argon2 time.
Rates use earliest ClientHello to latest verified AuthOK on the shared monotonic clock; scheduling spread remains visible.
No warm-up or failed sample filtering; one extra measured TCP peer with failed harness cleanup remains separately retained.
Initial source-manifest argument overflow and interrupted per-file evidence transfer are retained, not product authentication failures.
Server CPU measured over an enclosing sampler interval; 100 percent equals one logical CPU. RSS is sampled maximum, not kernel HWM.
Affinity 0-1 and nice 0 observed; no additional pinning. Governor availability and VM load/steal retained.
Peer uses contract-verified protocol/crypto core, not the full shipping client or its TUN/data plane; no deployed service changed.
